title: Creation of Patient-Specific Silicone Cardiac Models with Applications in Pre-surgical Plans and Hands-on Training
protocol: Obtain a patient radiologic imaging dataset, typically a CT or MRI.
Open the dataset in a computer aided design (CAD) segmentation software for segmenting patient anatomy.
Prepare an initial myocardial tissue segmentation using a Hounsfield unit threshold tool.
Set upper and lower HU limits according to dataset specifics.
Refine selection with tools such as crop, add and subtract, region grow, multi-slice edit, and cavity fill.
Right-click in the Project Manager area in Mimics and select New Mask.
Adjust mask settings in the generated dialogue box using pre-set anatomical windows or exact HU measurements.
Utilize the Hounsfield unit range of 226 to 3071 provided by the pre-set window to capture the blood pool.
Let a cardiologist, radiologist, or other subject matter expert review the virtual model segmentations.
Invert the myocardium segmentation using a cavity fill tool in the empty space around the myocardium segmentation.
Subtract the blood pool segmentation from the inverted myocardium using a Boolean subtract tool.
View the 3D rendering of the final blood pool and myocardial case segmentations.
Remove unnecessary blood vessels from the 3D blood pool model.
Select 3D Preview in Mimics.
Select the mask of interest in the Project Manager.
Choose the Edit Mask tool.
In the provided dialogue, select the Lasso tool.
Ensure that Remove is selected for editing.
Smooth the 3D myocardial case model using a smooth object tool.
Adjust iteration and smooth factor parameters as necessary.
Create a case model that is as smooth as possible without losing important anatomical details.
Export models in STL format for use in a 3D model editing software.
In Mimics, right-click on a specific mask and select Create Object.
Ensure the Optimal setting is selected and click Okay to create the object.
Smooth the generated model with five iterations at 0.4 mm smoothing.
Save/export the final 3D blood pool and myocardial case models as STL files.
Right-click the desired model and select STL+ to export an STL version of the model.
Open the myocardial case model STL file in a CAD program.
Render the visibility of the case in a transparent manner for clarity.
Trim excess myocardial case material from the model using a cut or punch tool.
Select approximately 0.5 cm between the outer edge of the case and the myocardium imprint on the inner wall.
In Magics, import the STLs through Import Part.
In the Project Management window, select the Transparent option for model rendering.
Use Cut > Indicate Polyline to select points of interest and trim excess material.
Apply the cut to finalize the digital mold.
Adjust the view of the myocardial case through rotation and panning tools to point the apex of the heart down and the aorta arch horizontal.
Make a horizontal cut through the aorta that divides the myocardial case into a lower half containing the apex and an upper half.
Cut > Indicate Polyline > select points of interest along the widest section of the lower half > Apply.
Cut > Indicate Polyline > select points of interest along the widest section of the upper half > Apply.
Add pegs to the myocardial case pieces to ensure proper alignment during assembly.
Use a prop generation tool and a Boolean subtraction tool with a clearance value of 0.25mm to create matching props and prop cavities.
Create a 1.0 cm diameter silicone fill hole in one of the myocardial case upper half pieces.
Verify hole placement with a SME to ensure it does not obscure vital external anatomical features.
Check diagnostics on all case pieces individually for errors such as inverted normal, bad edges, bad contours, near bad edges, planar holes, or shells.
Repair detected errors using a fixing tool/wizard if available.
For unresolved errors, use a shrink wrap tool in Magics to fix the issues.
Adjust shrink wrap sample interval and gap fill values as necessary to correct errors without altering physiology upon SME review.
Save/export the individual myocardial case pieces as STL files.
Create the physical molds.
Open the myocardial case and blood pool models in slicer software.
Produce 3D printing files (G-Code file) for an AM 3D printer.
Arrange pieces of the myocardial case using a rotate and/or lay flat tool.
Ensure any side that will meet up with another case piece is vertical.
Add 3D print supports to all pieces manually or using an automatic support generation tool.
Slice the models to generate G-code for use on the 3D printer.
Set heated bed temperature to 100°C and extruder temperature to 250°C for ABS material when printing blood pool.
Set infill density to 5% and default printing speed to 50 mm/s for blood pool.
Set inner shell speed to 70 mm/s and outer shell speed to 50 mm/s for blood pool.
Set heated bed temperature to 60 °C and extruder temperature to 205 °C for PLA material when printing myocardial mold.
Alternatively, set heated bed temperature to 100°C and extruder temperature to 250°C for ABS material when printing myocardial mold.
Set infill density to 15% and default printing speed to 50 mm/s for myocardial mold.
Set inner shell speed to 80 mm/s and outer shell speed to 30 mm/s for myocardial mold.
Save/export the G-code file.
Upload the printing file to the 3D printer using a Flash Drive or Wi-Fi connection, depending on the printer's capabilities.
Ensure correct filament is loaded onto the 3D printer.
Start the print process.
Remove all support material from the printed pieces using needle nose pliers and tweezers.
Assemble the myocardial case pieces around the blood pool mold.
Make small adjustments to the myocardial case mold piece using a handheld rotary sanding tool if necessary.
Edit the STL file in CAD software and create a new 3D print for large adjustments.
Use eye protection when using a handheld rotary sanding tool.
Avoid using a rotary sanding tool on the blood pool or myocardium case.
Perform an acetone vapor smooth if the myocardial case was printed with ABS and a smoother surface finish is desired.
Set up in a well-ventilated area away from open flames or sparks for acetone vapor smoothing.
Ensure plastic containers used do not contain PVC or polystyrene to avoid dissolution by acetone.
Line the bottom and sides of a container with paper towels.
Pour 30 mL of acetone onto the bottom paper towel.
Cover the bottom paper towel with a piece of aluminum foil.
Place myocardial case pieces onto the aluminum foil in the container.
Orient myocardial pieces so that the faces desired to be smoothed are vertical.
Ensure myocardial pieces do not touch each other or the paper towels on the wall of the container.
Place a lid on the container or cover with aluminum foil.
Allow myocardial case pieces to remain undisturbed in the container until ~80% of the desired surface finish is achieved, per visual inspection.
Check myocardial case pieces for the desired surface finish at 15 min intervals after an initial 30 min.
Carefully remove myocardial case pieces from the container touching only the outer surfaces when smoothness is achieved.
Allow the pieces to completely de-gas in a well-ventilated area for ~30 min, or until dry and hard.
Estimate the amount of two-part platinum cure silicone needed for the myocardial model.
Alternatively, measure the volume of the myocardium segmentation using CAD software to determine the amount of silicone needed.
Ensure the silicone has a shore hardness of 2 A.
Confirm the tensile strength is 1,986 kPa.
Verify the elongation at break is 763%.
Check that shrinkage is less than 0.0254 mm/mm.
Ensure the mixed viscosity is 18,000 cps.
Confirm the pot life is 12 min.
Verify the cure time is 40 min.
This study required 300 mL of silicone.
Thoroughly agitate part A and part B of the silicone before mixing.
Pour 150 mL of Part A and 150 mL of Part B into a mixing cup.
Add Sil-pigment product color "blood" to achieve desired color.
Mix all parts thoroughly by hand or with an agitator.
Place the mixed silicone into a vacuum chamber at 29 in Hg for 2-3 min.
Vent and remove de-gassed silicone from the chamber.
Submerge the blood pool in the silicone to ensure thorough coating.
Ensure all voids and cavities in the blood pool are filled with silicone.
Thoroughly spray all pieces of the myocardial case with an easy release product in a well-ventilated area.
Assemble the lower half of myocardial case around the apex of the blood pool.
Seal any seams between myocardial case pieces that allow silicone to leak out on the external surface.
Pour silicone into the space between the blood pool and case wall until gaps are filled.
Assemble remaining pieces of the myocardial case and secure tightly using rubber bands and clamps as necessary.
Pour silicone down the fill hole in the top of the myocardial case piece to ensure entire myocardial space is filled with silicone.
Allow the silicone to set for approximately 40 minutes.
Remove the silicone heart from the myocardial case and trim off any silicone seams created by case pieces or fill holes.
Identify all blood vessels that should have open ends on the silicone model and trim away covering silicone to expose the ABS blood pool inside.
Submerge the silicone heart in an acetone bath to dissolve the ABS.
Remove large chunks of ABS with tweezers as it softens 10-15 minutes after submersion.
Perform two to three additional acetone rinses/soaks with clean acetone.
Remove the cardiac model from the acetone bath.
Allow the remaining acetone to evaporate in a well-ventilated area.
